title: Bureau of Labor Statistics Public Data API
questions: brief on the latest jobs report
median wage for software developers by state

key_only: 50 series and 20 years per query instead of 25 and 10
BLS's own net and percent changes (calculations)

limits.note: v2 with a key: 500 queries a day, 50 series and 20 years per query; v1 without: 25, 25 and 10; 50 requests per 10 seconds either way. fetch.py splits requests and counts queries in ~/.bls/usage.json.

manual.how: Run --manual-bundle (or follow --check): it writes INSTRUCTIONS.md, spec.json and the self-contained download_bls.sh / .ps1 (the requests built in) into <out>/manual_download/bls/. On a computer with internet access run one script with one command (it asks for a key with hidden input only when the request needs one), then upload the response_NN.json files and run --ingest. Without the scripts: https://data.bls.gov/dataQuery/find or a series page https://data.bls.gov/timeseries/<ID> lets you download one series at a time as XLSX, but --ingest reads only API JSON responses.

cache.why: Small queries under a daily quota; <out>/data/bls/ is reused within a run (route reuse_existing). Data are revised monthly, so no cross-run cache.

redistribution.why: BLS data are U.S. government works in the public domain (17 U.S.C. 105). The API terms of service (https://www.bls.gov/developers/termsOfService.htm) require stating the retrieval date and the statement in notices, and forbid using the BLS logo; the data and raw responses may go in a replication package.

notices: BLS.gov cannot vouch for the data or analyses derived from these data after the data have been retrieved from BLS.gov.
citation: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, {dataset}, retrieved {retrieved_long} through the BLS Public Data API (https://www.bls.gov/developers/).

audit_hooks.why: BLS terms of service: state the date the data were retrieved; BLS revises CES, LAUS and seasonal factors.
BLS terms of service require the statement in notices wherever BLS data are published.
BLS flags recent CES, JOLTS and LAUS values preliminary (footnote P); a product citing them must say so.
BLS footnotes some annual averages as covering fewer months (2025 CPS-based averages exclude October 2025, which was not collected); a product citing them must say so.
The retrieval date, API version and exact queries are needed to state the data vintage and to reproduce the pull.

clarify: Which measure? Unemployment: U-3 (official, LNS14000000) or U-6 (LNS13327709). Wages: average hourly earnings (CES), median weekly earnings (CPS) or the ECI. Inflation: CPI-U headline or core, CPI-W, chained CPI-U. Default: the measure BLS leads with in its news release (U-3, CES payrolls, CPI-U headline).
Seasonally adjusted or not? Default: SA for monthly changes and charts; NSA for 12-month CPI changes and annual averages (BLS's own convention).

Which period and baseline (since February 2020, the last 10 years, calendar years)? Default: the business-cycle peak before the event asked about, otherwise the latest 10 years; show one alternative baseline as a sensitivity.

Nominal or real, and which deflator? Default: real, deflated as BLS does it: CPI-W for production and nonsupervisory employees (CES0500000032), CPI-U for all employees (CES0500000013) and other groups, in dollars of the latest full year; say which.
